$comment: SWEEP LEDGER for cinatra-ai/docs#160 (AC5, AC10). Committed beside the gate config it belongs to. Section 1 lists every unique occurrence the widened engine found on the published pages before the sweep, keyed by file + SOURCE line, with the pattern classes that fired on it and its disposition. Section 2 inventories every in-page CI-directive comment with a measured retain-or-remove decision. Both sections are GENERATED FROM EVIDENCE, not hand-written: section 1 by running the engine over the pre-sweep bytes of each touched file, section 2 by removing each marker in turn and diffing the owning gate's findings.

contentSweep.$comment: One source line can carry several pattern classes, so the class totals below exceed the unique-occurrence count. That is the reconciliation AC5 asks for: uniqueOccurrences is the number of LINES changed, classTotals counts MATCHES by class.

reconciliationAgainstTheIssue.$comment: docs#160 quotes 37 work-item citations, 16 ruling citations and 10 editorial / publish-status annotations across the Application Design HTML pages. Those figures were produced by hand-sampling the pages; the figures above are produced by the ENGINE, so they differ, and the differences are recorded here rather than reconciled away.
whyTheyDiffer: COUNTING UNIT. The issue counts CITATIONS; the engine counts unique OCCURRENCES (file + source line) and, separately, MATCHES. One line can carry three `cinatra#1883` citations, which is three citations but one occurrence and three matches. classTotals above counts matches; uniqueOccurrences counts lines.

THE ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION CLASS IS SEPARATE HERE. The issue folds `AC6`-style citations into its narrative; the engine patterns them as their own class (18 line-level occurrences on the HTML pages), so they are neither in the 37 nor in the 16.

MARKDOWN IS INCLUDED. 13 Markdown occurrences were swept under the AC4 decision (the qualified work-item form is now patterned). The issue lists 12 of them; the 13th, references/platform/extensions.md `pre-#118`, was found by the engine and is recorded above like any other.

ONE ISSUE-LISTED PAGE NEEDED NO EDIT. The issue's Gap-2 samples name four pages; the engine agrees exactly — artifacts, permissions, extensions and notifications — and confirms design-system, application-design-components and application-design-connectors were already clean.

ciDirectiveComments.$comment: AC10. Each marker was probed individually: remove it, re-run the gate that owns it exactly as this repo's CI runs it (profile ops-docs, this repo's .github/source-leak-gate.json), and diff the findings. A marker whose removal adds a finding on its own line is load-bearing and is RETAINED; one whose removal changes nothing suppresses nothing and is REMOVED. Verified collectively as well as individually: the gate reports the same 12 findings before and after the removals. RESIDUAL RISK, recorded: the source-leak rules live in cinatra-ai/ci and are SHA-pinned by this repo's caller; a future rule widening could make a removed marker's line fire, and the fix is to re-add that marker with fresh probe evidence.
